why: RFC-0002 section 4.2 / RFC-0047 / RFC-0079 -- the SchedContext surface, which ROS 2 has no counterpart for at all. A mixed-criticality image runs a 20 ms control loop and best-effort telemetry on ONE executor on ONE RTOS task, so the criticality ordering has to live in user space: N callbacks must not cost N kernel priority slots (RFC-0002 non-goal 3), and RFC-0079 exists because the raw kernel number is unwritable by hand -- each RTOS has its own range and its own DIRECTION. rclcpp's nearest answer is one `MultiThreadedExecutor` thread per priority, which an MCU cannot pay for. A `uint8_t` index into the executor's SchedContext table, not a pointer -- the table is static and an id survives being copied into an options struct before the context exists.
